fullPassage: While newborns do not seem to be stressed when their parents walk out of the room, infants around one year old often cry uncontrollably even if their parents are gone for just a short while. What changes occur between these stages? Object recognition and retention turn out to be the key. For the first couple of months of life, the cognitive abilities of babies are still developing, and their understanding that objects continue to exist even when they are out of sight has not yet formed. Newborns believe that the only things that exist are those they can see. Consequently, when their parents leave their view, they do not experience distress because they cannot fully grasp the significance of the absence of their parents for them, out of sight means out of existence. However, as they grow, infants begin to be able to perceive objects and mentally represent them even when those objects are not directly visible. So the absence of their parents now takes on a new meaning; they are not where they are supposed to be. It is this awareness that triggers feelings of anxiety during the period of separation.
